This paper asks a simple question: can we make a sample much larger without changing its shape? Expansion microscopy helps us see small structures by physically expanding a sample. However, a large expansion factor alone does not tell us whether the expansion is uniform. The researchers developed a method called high-fold homogeneous expansion microscopy. They reported about eight- to nine-fold expansion in a single round and tested structural preservation in centrioles and nuclear pore complexes. The method also supports labeling after expansion. The main point is to check both how much a sample expands and how well its structure is preserved.
